subject: literature
passage: Aunt Beatriz never threw anything away. Rubber bands were wound into a ball on the kitchen windowsill, empty jars lined the pantry shelves, and newspapers from years past were stacked in the hallway "in case they come in handy." ______ to her, every object, no matter how worn or ordinary, was something that might one day prove useful.
stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

explanation.why: The text shows Aunt Beatriz keeping things "in case they come in handy." The last sentence puts that same idea in general terms: she believes any object might one day be useful. A restatement transition is needed.
explanation.A: Incorrect. Her belief is the reason she keeps things, not a result of keeping them.
explanation.B: Incorrect. The examples (rubber bands, jars, newspapers) came before; the last sentence is a general statement, not another example.
explanation.C: Incorrect. "Still" signals a contrast, but her belief fits her habit of keeping everything.
explanation.D: Correct. "In other words" signals that the last sentence restates, in general terms, why she keeps things "in case they come in handy."
